slides.headline: Angry client email? Don't reply yet.

slides.label: THE MISTAKE
slides.wrong_sub: You write what you feel, not what helps.
slides.right: Let AI cool it down first.

slides.label: Step 1
slides.title: Find what they want
slides.card: Here is a client's email: [paste]. What do they actually want? What are they worried about?
slides.note: Remove names and private details first.

slides.label: Step 2
slides.title: Check the facts
slides.card: List what they claim. Mark each: true, false or unclear, based on my notes. [paste notes]

slides.label: Step 3
slides.title: Draft 3 replies
slides.card: Write 3 replies: firm, friendly and a middle ground. Keep each under 100 words. No blame.

slides.label: Step 4
slides.title: Find the fix
slides.card: What is one concrete next step I can offer, with a date, that would calm this down?

slides.label: Step 5
slides.title: Sound like you
slides.card: Rewrite this reply in my voice. Short sentences. Keep it calm. Remove anything defensive.
slides.note: Read it out loud. Then send it yourself.

scenes.headline: You saved that video. Never watched it.

scenes.title: Get the transcript
scenes.footer: No transcript? Try a different video.

scenes.title: THE PROMPT
scenes.label: COPY THIS
scenes.text: Here is a video transcript. Give me the 5 key ideas, 3 things to try this week and any claims I should fact-check. Skip the intro and sponsor parts. Ask me if anything is unclear.
Follow for Part 2: ask the video questions.
scenes.note: Check key claims. Transcripts can contain errors.
